sentences.text: the use of technology around the world to feature in the IT Club's online magazine.
Listen to the information and complete the notes below.
You now have one minute to tidy up your answers.
you found in Rachel?
OK. I'll go first.
I was reading this interesting article about Youth Boost centers in South Africa that have been set up by the local government.
OK, so these Youth Boost centers are they the teenagers?
Yeah, mainly for young people without a job and who aren't at college.
And they join in the center of members, So why do they sign up?
Well, they can like learn loads of different things like, the centers give them lots of practical advice on things like how to start their own companies.
Sounds good. I've always wanted to start my own company!
I think I'd like that much more than a boring office job or something.
Yeah, totally. Me too.
They also help them learn new workplace skills.
Things like, writing emails.
You know, that sort of thing.
it does sound good.
But offering things like workplace skills isn’t that just like any other job centre?
What's just got to do with technology?
Well. this one is special.
The The centres themselves are entirely cash free, and young people who join can earn virtual money called Imali, which means money in Zulu apparently.
You can spend it there.
At the centre.
So, do they use computers to earn it, just like Bitcoin?
No, no. They earn this Imali in lots of different ways.
One of the things they can do is local volunteering.
And they can do any kind of volunteering, as long as it’s in the local area.
Like they might help out a nearby school or help the old people in the community.
The other thing they can do is go to personal development workshops.
So they earn for attending?
Yeah. That's nice.
And what do they learn about these workshops?
You know, like how to not give up when you're dealing with a problem.
Or how to set yourself goals.
Things like that.
That sounds pretty cool.
What can they buy with this.
what's its name?
Imali! Imali! Well, as I said, the of cash free, but they can use Imali at the centre cafes to buy things like snacks.
They can also use the money to pay for online courses.
Can they work on the courses at home, too?
I think so, but the centres have computers so apparently most people prefer to spend time there.
Sounds great.
I mean, that they can buy with Imanli.
Yeah, the other online option is that you can donate Imanli's to charity.
Does that mean the charity gets Imanli's?
But how is that useful?
No, no the Youth booth Centre gives the charities real money.
Hmm, but members, they don’t earn actual money, but they still like it?
Apparently so. So what's the big attraction?
Well, from what it said in the article it’s just a place where they can feel a sense of belonging.
Oh, that's really nice.
OK, so it would be good to write in the article what we think.
Let's talk about the good points first.
Rachel, you were researching it, what do you reckon?
I think they're an excellent idea, mainly because they give people a way to give back to the community.
So, it’s more than just basic welfare.
Yeah, I was thinking the same.
What do you think, Aaron?
From what Rachel was saying, I think the best thing seems to be that it lets people learn life skills like having to deal with money.
Alright. What about the cons?
Well, the obvious problem that I can see is that actual money is more useful.
People need real money to spend on meals, not just snacks, especially if they need to help their families.
Yes, that’s a very good point.
What about you, Aaron?
What do you think?
Well, again, from what Rachel said so far, it’s hard to see any bad points.
Maybe the only downside I can think of would be it might be vulnerable to hacking.
you know, because, well, someone could hack into it online.
